articles.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Vision, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can simultaneously process code repositories, visual diagrams, and spoken instructions in a single inference pass. Benchmarks show a 40% improvement on SWE-Bench and near-human performance on graduate-level scientific reasoning tasks, signaling a major step toward general-purpose AI assistants for professional workflows.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2 solved 88% of International Mathematical Olympiad problems from the past decade, up from 72% in earlier iterations. The model uses a novel chain-of-verification architecture that self-checks intermediate proof steps, reducing hallucinated reasoning chains and making it a credible tool for formal mathematics research.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Amazon Fulfillment Centers
articles.summary: Tesla's third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has started pilot deployments at select Amazon warehouses, performing bin-picking, pallet stacking, and inventory scanning tasks. The robots leverage on-device vision-language models for real-time task adaptation, reportedly handling 85% of targeted warehouse tasks without human intervention, raising both productivity hopes and workforce displacement concerns.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform with Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics officially launched the commercial Atlas platform featuring new hands with 22 degrees of freedom and force-feedback tactile sensors, enabling fine manipulation tasks like connector insertion and tool use. The system runs on a hybrid reinforcement-learning and model-predictive-control stack, targeting automotive manufacturing and construction applications with a 2027 volume production timeline.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 with 1 Trillion Parameters and Mixture-of-Depths Architecture
articles.summary: Meta released Llama 4 under a permissive open license, introducing a mixture-of-depths architecture that dynamically allocates compute across transformer layers based on input complexity. Early community benchmarks show it matching proprietary frontier models on coding and reasoning tasks while running efficiently on clusters of consumer-grade GPUs, dramatically lowering the barrier to state-of-the-art AI deployment.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm GAA Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC announced that its N1.4 process node using gate-all-around transistor architecture has entered risk production three months ahead of the original roadmap. The node promises a 25% performance gain and 35% power reduction over N2, with early wafers showing competitive yields, positioning TSMC to supply next-generation AI accelerator and mobile SoC customers by late 2027.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Trials
articles.summary: Neuralink secured FDA approval to begin human trials of its N2 implant, which doubles electrode density to 2,048 channels and introduces bidirectional stimulation capabilities. The expanded trial will enroll 50 patients with spinal cord injuries and ALS, aiming to demonstrate not only motor intent decoding but also rudimentary sensory feedback, a critical milestone for closed-loop neuroprosthetics.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C to Scale Humanoid Robot Production for Industrial Clients
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a $1.5 billion Series C round led by Microsoft and Saudi Aramco's venture arm, valuing the company at $12 billion. The funding will expand its manufacturing facility in South Carolina to produce 10,000 Figure 03 humanoid units annually, targeting automotive assembly, logistics, and energy sector deployments where labor shortages are most acute.
